question.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡1 & (\text{mod}\,2) \\ x≡4 & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $2$ and $5$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $2\cdot 5=10.$

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,2)\,⟹\,x=1+2t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 1+2t & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 2t & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $5$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $3\cdot 2≡1\,(\text{mod}\,5).$ So, we multiply both sides by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2t & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 3\cdot 2t & ≡3\cdot 3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ t & ≡9 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ t & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=4+5s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =1+2t \\  & =1+2(4+5s) \\  & =9+10s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡9\,(\text{mod}\,10)$ is the unique solution modulo $10,$ and $x=9$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
